_comment: HOW EVERY SURFACE MUST READ A RUNTIME, DECLARED ONCE (#377).
apps/open-swe and apps/example each implement the runtime axis, and nothing
asserted they agree. That is not hypothetical: before #360 open-swe coerced
an unrecognised runtime to fastapi and example coerced it to django, so THE
SAME MALFORMED REQUEST WAS ANSWERED BY A DIFFERENT PLANE depending on which
surface sent it, and neither said so. It stood for months.
The copies agree today because one author wrote both within hours. THE
ABSENCE OF DRIFT IS NOT THE ABSENCE OF THE DEFECT, IT IS THE ABSENCE OF
ELAPSED TIME — and measured before this file existed, apps/example could be
reverted to the exact pre-#360 behaviour with its whole suite still green:
coerce EVERYTHING to django          4 failed   (resolution was pinned)
coerce only UNKNOWN to fastapi     127 passed   (refusal was not)
stop refusing a MISSING runtime    127 passed   (nor was absence)
So this file is CASES, not a list. A checker comparing the three copies of
RUNTIMES would ship green and stay green while the two PARSERS diverged on
what parsers actually diverge on: casing, whitespace, unknown and absent.
It would name the property and be unable to fail for the reason the
property matters.
REFUSAL CASES ARE THE POINT. A fixture of happy-path rows is satisfied by
two parsers that both silently fall through to the same default, which is
agreement about nothing. A component that defaults on malformed input
reports having considered a question it did not consider.
CONSUMED BEHAVIOURALLY BY BOTH PLANES, through whatever surface each one
exposes — open-swe calls its exported parseRuntime, example POSTs to its
route because its copy is private. Neither reads the other's source, and
they share no module, so a divergence planted in one turns exactly one red.
That independence is asserted by mutation and recorded in the PR.
OMITTING `input` MEANS UNDEFINED. JSON has no undefined, and 'absent' is a
case this axis must distinguish from every other, so it is spelled by the
key not being there rather than by a sentinel that could be mistaken for a
value.

cases.why: django is served by both surfaces
node — the TypeScript plane, which was unreachable until #360
ABSENT expresses no preference and must refuse rather than default — this is the case that was coerced for months
null is absent, not a runtime named null
the empty string is absent too — an operator who names nothing has named nothing
an unrecognised runtime is NAMED, not coerced — and unknown is a different answer from missing
CASING IS NOT NORMALISED. Two parsers silently disagreeing about whether DJANGO is django is exactly the drift a list-comparison checker cannot see
nor is whitespace trimmed — a leading space is a different string and must not resolve
a trailing space likewise, because trimming one end and not the other is how two copies drift apart
a non-string is unknown rather than a crash — this arrives from a request body
a runtime-shaped substring is not a runtime
